SC families can receive ₹2 lakh for house renovation and completion.
ST families can receive up to ₹2.50 lakh under the separate programme.
The Keralam SAFE Scheme (Secure Accommodation and Facility Enhancement Scheme) provides financial assistance to eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) families to renovate damaged houses or complete unfinished houses. The scheme aims to improve housing conditions and help eligible families make their homes safer and suitable for living. The SC and ST programmes operate under their respective development departments and follow separate eligibility conditions. The same department also runs the Dakshayani Self-Entrepreneurship Assistance Scheme for SC women's self-help groups, and the UNNATHI Scholarship Scheme for SC/ST students pursuing overseas studies.
Under the SAFE Housing Scheme, eligible SC families can receive ₹2 lakh for house renovation and completion. The assistance is paid in three instalments of ₹50,000, ₹1 lakh and ₹50,000, subject to construction progress and verification. Applicants must belong to the SC category, have an annual family income of up to ₹1 lakh, and own a house registered in their name or their spouse's name. The house construction must have been completed after 1 April 2010.
Under this scheme, the eligible ST families can receive financial assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh per house, based on the approved estimate. Applicants must belong to the ST category and have an annual family income below ₹2.50 lakh. The programme supports the renovation of dilapidated houses and completion of unfinished houses, subject to the applicable departmental guidelines.
Eligible applicants can apply for the Keralam SAFE scheme offline. For this, SC applicants should contact the concerned Block, Municipality or Corporation Scheduled Caste Development Office to obtain the application form and confirm the current submission deadline. They must submit the completed form with the required documents and house renovation estimate. The department verifies the application, and an accredited engineer inspects the house and prepares the estimate before the final beneficiary list receives approval. ST applicants should contact the nearest Tribal Development Office to obtain the applicable guidelines, confirm the required documents and submit their application through the prescribed online or offline process.
The Keralam SAFE (Secure Accommodation and Facility Enhancement) Scheme supports eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) families in renovating damaged houses and completing unfinished homes. The assistance amount and applicable conditions differ between the two programmes.
Financial assistance of up to ₹2 lakh is sanctioned for house completion and renovation
The assistance is released in three instalments of ₹50,000, ₹1,00,000 and ₹50,000.
Beneficiaries can use the assistance for roof completion, sanitary toilet construction, wall strengthening, installation of doors and windows, and kitchen renovation.
Approved works also include flooring, plastering, whitewashing, painting, electrical work and plumbing.
Eligible households can receive financial assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh per house, based on the approved estimate.
The assistance supports the renovation of dilapidated houses and completion of unfinished houses.
Priority is given to eligible flood-affected families and families identified through the Extreme Poverty Survey 2021–22 and the specified micro-planning e-survey.
Gothrajeevika tribal self-help groups engaged in construction activities receive preference for house repair and renovation work.
The department's published guidelines provide for 25% of the funds to go to women beneficiaries.
The Keralam SAFE Scheme supports eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) families in improving their existing houses and completing unfinished homes. The approved construction and renovation works should follow the guidelines issued by the respective development department.
According to the government order dated 27 September 2022, SC beneficiaries can use the assistance for the following construction and renovation components:
Kitchen renovation, including kitchen slabs, shelves and cooking facilities
Plastering, whitewashing and wall painting
Electrical work, including wiring, ELCB, fans and lights
Plumbing to provide piped water to the kitchen and toilet
The Scheduled Tribes Development Department's SAFE housing programme supports the following broad categories of work:
Repair and renovation of dilapidated houses
Note: The Scheduled Caste notice provides the detailed list of renovation works. The Scheduled Tribes Development Department confirms the broader purpose of its SAFE programme, but applicants should verify the specific eligible works with the department before undertaking construction.
The Keralam SAFE Scheme provides housing renovation and completion assistance to eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) families. Applicants must meet the eligibility conditions prescribed by the respective development department.
The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste category.
The applicant's annual family income must not exceed ₹1 lakh.
The house construction must have been completed after 1 April 2010.
The house must be registered in the applicant's name or their spouse's name.
The applicant must not have received government financial assistance for house construction, renovation or completion during the previous five years.
Applicants who received the final instalment of housing assistance within the previous five years are not eligible.
The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Tribe category.
The applicant's annual family income must be below ₹2.50 lakh.
The house must have been completed after 1 April 2006, subject to confirmation of the applicable conditions under the ST programme.
The applicant's family must not have received government financial assistance for house renovation or completion after 1 April 2018.
Eligible families may receive priority according to the department's prescribed criteria, including applicable flood-affected family and poverty-survey provisions.
Note: The SC eligibility conditions are based on the notice shared. The ST conditions come from the separately published Scheduled Tribes Development Department guidelines. Applicants should confirm the latest eligibility rules with the relevant department before applying.
Applicants should prepare the following documents to apply for housing renovation or completion assistance under the Keralam SAFE Scheme. The caste certificate and income certificate must correspond to the applicant's category and applicable eligibility conditions.
Scheduled Caste (SC) Certificate or Scheduled Tribe (ST) Certificate
Aadhaar Card or other accepted identity proof
House Renovation or Construction Estimate
Photographs of the Existing House, if required
Declaration Regarding Previous Housing Assistance, if required
Other Supporting Documents Required by the Concerned Department
Note: This is a provisional list. Applicants should confirm the mandatory documents with the concerned Scheduled Caste Development Department or Scheduled Tribes Development Department before applying.
Eligible applicants must follow the application procedure prescribed by the concerned department to receive housing renovation or completion assistance under the Keralam SAFE Scheme. The application process differs for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) beneficiaries.
Visit the Scheduled Caste Development Office at your concerned Block, Municipality or Corporation.
Obtain the SAFE Scheme application form from the concerned office.
Fill in the application form with the required personal, family income and house details.
Attach the required documents, including the caste certificate, income certificate and house-related documents.
Submit the completed application form and supporting documents to the concerned office by 31 October 2026.
Keep the application acknowledgement for future reference and contact the office to check the application status.
Contact the nearest Tribal Development Office to confirm the application procedure for the ST housing assistance programme.
Obtain the application form and scheme guidelines from the concerned office or the official department website.
Complete the application form and provide the required personal, income and housing details.
Attach the documents required by the Scheduled Tribes Development Department.
Submit the application through the prescribed online or offline method.
Keep the acknowledgement or application reference number and follow up with the concerned office regarding verification and approval.
Important: The SC programme's application instructions and deadline should be confirmed with the concerned Scheduled Caste Development Office. For ST applicants, the department's official website states that applications for its schemes may be submitted online or manually at the nearest Tribal Development Office, depending on the individual scheme.

The Keralam SAFE Scheme provides financial assistance to eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) families to renovate damaged houses or complete unfinished houses.
2. How much financial assistance is available under the Keralam SAFE Scheme?
Eligible SC families can receive ₹2 lakh, while eligible ST families can receive assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh under the separate programme.
3. Who is eligible for the Keralam SAFE Scheme?
Eligible SC families must have an annual family income of up to ₹1 lakh and meet the applicable housing conditions. Eligible ST families must have an annual family income below ₹2.50 lakh and satisfy the requirements of their programme.
4. What works are covered under the Keralam SAFE Scheme?
The scheme supports approved house renovation and completion works, including roof completion, wall strengthening, kitchen renovation, toilet construction, flooring, electrical work and plumbing, subject to the applicable departmental guidelines.
5. How can I apply for the Keralam SAFE Scheme?
SC applicants can contact their concerned Block, Municipality or Corporation Scheduled Caste Development Office. ST applicants should approach the relevant Tribal Development Office to confirm the application procedure and required documents.
6. What is the last date to apply for the Keralam SAFE Scheme?
The last date to submit applications for SC applicants is 31 October 2026. ST applicants should confirm the application deadline with the concerned Tribal Development Office.
7. Does an SC applicant need to submit a cost estimate with the SAFE application?
No. A simple statement describing the needed work is enough at the time of application. An accredited engineer visits the house afterward and prepares the formal estimate.
8. What happens if an SC beneficiary's roof is still incomplete when it's time for the next installment?
Funds are released specifically for roof concreting first. The remaining approved work is completed once the roof is finished, and the final installment is released only after all work is complete.
9. Is there a cap on toilet-construction costs under the SC component of SAFE?
Yes. Toilet construction is capped at ₹40,000 within the overall estimate, even though total assistance can go up to ₹2 lakh.
10. How are SC applicants ranked when more people apply than funds allow in a year?
Applicants are scored out of 10 points using criteria such as woman-headed families, students in the house, and house size. Higher-scoring applicants get priority, and ties are broken in favour of the applicant with lower income.
11. Can a family that already received flood relief assistance still apply for SAFE?
Yes. Families that received up to ₹1 lakh in government distress or relief assistance, such as flood relief, remain eligible for the SC component of SAFE.
